reason: The score charges a contact pose twice: it loses the reach point and adds 100 x 1/N_evaluated to the contact term. A pose a hard stop removes is not evaluated, so it costs reach only. A stop that blocks a pose the chain would press into the skin therefore scores better than the metal that blocks it, although the wearer is blocked either way. Held out, the upper stop J3MAX 122.74 is placed on the fast bench and is inert on the exact bench. It cuts 3 held poses (752 / 897 / 965, all overhead at elev 150-165) whose metal would be 2.0-3.4 mm in the skin. As contacts they would move the held contact term from 14/875 to 17/878, which is +0.34 points (held 22.72, not 22.38), and the held edge over the lead would shrink from 1.07 to about 0.73. On the bench the 6 stopped poses would also clash the E strap against link 2 (a parts failure, which costs no contact), so the lower stop relabels a limit the chain already has. The dowel is the honest, buildable version of that limit (verifier C1-C3), so this is watch, not gamed. Proposed catalogue entry T6, below.
